paper_title: 2-Tier SimCSE Elevating BERT for Robust Sentence Embeddings
caption: : Figure 2: Accuracy comparison of different models on paraphrase sentiment, and STS tasks.
model_annotation: This bar chart, labeled as Figure 2 from the paper “2-Tier SimCSE: Elevating BERT for Robust Sentence Embeddings,” compares the performance of five different model configurations across three evaluation metrics: Sentiment Accuracy (light yellow), STS Correlation (light pink), and Paraphrase Accuracy (light blue), as indicated in the legend. The horizontal axis lists the model variants in order: Single-task_baseline, Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout, Unsupervised_SimCSE, Supervised_SimCSE, and 2-Tier SimCSE. The vertical axis, labeled “Accuracy / Correlation,” ranges from 0 to 0.8 with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. For each model, three adjacent bars represent the respective metric scores. The 2-Tier SimCSE model achieves the highest scores across all three metrics: approximately 0.51 for Sentiment Accuracy, 0.82 for STS Correlation, and 0.79 for Paraphrase Accuracy. The Supervised_SimCSE model follows closely, particularly excelling in STS Correlation (~0.81) and Paraphrase Accuracy (~0.78), while the Single-task_baseline and Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout models show lower performance across the board, with Paraphrase Accuracy consistently highest among the three metrics for all models. The Unsupervised_SimCSE model shows moderate performance, with STS Correlation (~0.72) and Paraphrase Accuracy (~0.78) notably higher than its Sentiment Accuracy (~0.53). The chart visually emphasizes the performance gains of the 2-Tier SimCSE approach over prior baselines and SimCSE variants.
